description_full: Life Time Group Holdings, Inc., through its subsidiaries, provides health, fitness, and wellness experiences to a community of individual members in the United States and Canada. The company offers fitness floors with equipment, locker rooms, group fitness studios, cycle, yoga, pilates studios, bar and lounge, free weight and resistance equipment, cardiovascular equipment, steam room and sauna, cold plunges, racquetball and squash spaces, recovery spaces, indoor and outdoor pools and bistros, indoor and outdoor tennis and pickleball courts, basketball, volleyball courts, LifeSpa, LifeCafe, and childcare and kids academy learning spaces. It also provides dynamic personal training, dynamic stretch, small group training, weight loss coaching, nutrition coaching, medi-spa, physical therapy and chiropractic, assessments and lab testing, sport specific coaching, endurance coaching, swim lessons and team coaching, towel and locker service, experience life, and ARORA and MIORA community services. In addition, the company engages in athletic leagues and tournaments, athletic events, LT Games, social events, outdoor group runs, outdoor group cycle rides, and charity events; organizing kids' birthday parties, parents night out, summer and vacation camps for kids, sports training camps, swim meets, charity events; and providing nutritional supplements and apparels, as well as designing, building, and operating of sports and athletic, professional fitness, family recreation, and spa centers in a resort-like environment in suburban and urban locations of metropolitan areas. Further, its digital platform provides live streaming fitness classes, remote goal-based personal training, nutrition and weight loss support, curated award-winning health, and fitness and wellness content. The company was formerly known as LTF Holdings, Inc. and changed its name to Life Time Group Holdings, Inc. in June 21, 2021. The company was founded in 1992 and is headquartered in Chanhassen, Minnesota.

financial_summary: Life Time Group Holdings, Inc. is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $10.4B market cap on $3.0B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +18% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +13.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 4% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
The company is burning through $21M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.7× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 5.6×.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 8.5% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 16% operating margin runs 9pp above the Consumer Cyclical median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 56% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 4% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 38% and a beta of 1.32, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.49 vs 5y 1.53), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $115.5M traded a day.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $22.24 (margin of safety -109%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 12%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $11.73 to $39.85 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks expensive against Consumer Cyclical peers: P/E 25.1 vs 18.8 and EV/EBITDA 16.1 vs 10.7 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of -0.2% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.4% (vs the 8% bar).
The 15 covering analysts target $57.60 on average, 24% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 23.6% annual cash-flow growth, 11pp more than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 4% falls short of the cost of capital of 10.2%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 3.35).
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 2.33x.
ROE of 12% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.6x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 14pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 1.7% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 1.7x net debt to EBITDA ($204.8M of cash against $1.5B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 5.6x.
The current ratio of 0.63 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 18.0% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 4.5% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Capex runs 3.0x depreciation (29.8% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 8.9% on average.
own: Insiders own 8.5%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 96%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (20 sales, net $1.2B sold).
The share count has grown 3.1% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 46,000 employees, each generates about $65K of revenue, 0.2x the Consumer Cyclical median, and revenue has grown 22.8% a year across its filed history.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $1.7M (26x revenue per employee).
